headline: Anthropic founded by ex-OpenAI researchers led by the Amodeis
summary: Anthropic was founded at the beginning of 2021 (Delaware entity date January 26, 2021) by former OpenAI staff, with Dario Amodei as CEO and Daniela Amodei as President, alongside co-founders Jack Clark, Jared Kaplan, Tom Brown, Chris Olah, Sam McCandlish and Ben Mann.

source.title: Anthropic raises Series B to build robust AI

extracted.governance: Founded as a public benefit corporation; mission framed as AI safety and research ('steerable, interpretable, robust' systems).
extracted.moat: Founding team wrote the GPT-3 and scaling-laws work at OpenAI (per Core Views page).
extracted.strategy: Initially research-first; commercialization 'down the road' (TechCrunch, May 2021).

notes: Anthropic's own T1 text says only 'founding at the beginning of 2021'; the Jan 26, 2021 date comes from a T4 SAM.gov-derived profile (cited by Wikipedia). Founder list is from T4 sources (Wikipedia citing CNBC 2025 and Reuters 2023, which I could not open); Anthropic sometimes describes seven co-founders. Contrary Research says 'December 2020' and that 15 researchers left OpenAI — see conflicts.

headline: Reuters: 47% of Anthropic 2025 sales routed via Amazon and Google; $3.8B consumption vs $789M subscription
summary: Reuters, from the confidential IPO filing, reported Anthropic routed 47% of 2025 sales (about $2.16B) through Amazon and Google cloud marketplaces, up from 11% in 2023 and 32% in 2024, paying roughly 16 cents per dollar (~$351M) in distribution fees.

source.title: Exclusive-Anthropic IPO prospectus lays bare deep dependence on Big Tech partners

extracted.customers: two unnamed customers ~12% of FY2025 revenue each; most large customers lack long-term contracts

notes: Four outlets (Calcalist, TradingKey, Investing.com, Yahoo) reproduce the Reuters text; Reuters computed the ~$351M fee. Usage-based revenue $3.8B and subscription $789M sum to the $4.59B total (subscription ~17%). Marketplace sales are booked GROSS as revenue (Anthropic is principal) with the platform share booked as a marketing expense, so the >80% pre-partner-share gross margin and the revenue total both include the channel economics. Two customers each generated 12% of revenue with no long-term contracts. Cloud providers collected 60% of the $909M of bills outstanding at end-2025 (42% in 2024). $54.6B non-cancellable hosting/compute commitments at end-2025; total long-term commitments >$417B in early 2026.
